questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary objective of scan chains in DFT?
options: To reduce power consumption during normal operation
To enable easy debugging of logic circuits
To enhance fault coverage by improving controllability and observability
To optimize clock domain crossings

questions.text: In an ATPG process, which fault model provides the highest correlation with actual silicon failures?
options: Stuck-at fault model
Transition delay fault model
Bridging fault model
Cell-aware fault model

questions.text: What is the main disadvantage of using a full scan design in DFT?
options: Increased power consumption during functional operation
Poor fault coverage compared to functional testing
Increased area overhead due to additional latches
Inability to detect path delay faults

questions.text: Which ATPG algorithm is commonly used for stuck-at fault testing and is known for its efficiency?
options: PODEM
D Algorithm
FAN Algorithm
Random Pattern Testing

questions.text: During ATPG, why is X-handling (unknown values) a major challenge in scan-based testing?
options: X-values cannot propagate through combinational logic
ATPG algorithms treat X-values as don’t-care, reducing test quality
X-values prevent accurate fault simulation and test pattern generation
X-values increase the power consumption of test patterns

questions.text: Which of the following is true about Built-In Self-Test (BIST) in DFT?
options: It requires an external ATPG tool for test pattern generation
It uses a Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) for test pattern generation
It completely eliminates the need for scan chains
It reduces the area overhead compared to external test solutions

questions.text: Why is launch-off-capture (LOC) preferred over launch-off-shift (LOS) in at-speed testing?
options: LOC provides better timing closure compared to LOS
LOC reduces the number of test patterns required for delay fault testing
LOC prevents excessive power consumption during at-speed testing
LOC eliminates hold-time violations in the design

questions.text: What is the primary function of the Test Access Port (TAP) in IEEE 1149.1 (JTAG)?
options: To provide access to internal nodes of the chip for debugging
To facilitate wafer-level testing only
To allow direct modification of functional logic states during operation
To reduce scan chain depth in large designs

questions.text:
In an MBIST (Memory Built-In Self-Test) architecture, which technique is commonly used for fault
detection?
options: March algorithms
PODEM algorithm
Stuck-at fault model
Bridging fault detection

questions.text: What is the primary advantage of using compression-based ATPG techniques like X-Compact?
options: Reduced test power consumption
Minimized dependence on scan chains
Significant reduction in test data volume and test application time
Improved defect tolerance compared to traditional ATPG
